skills.grammarMd:
With verbs that take an object (eat, see, say, do…) the past works differently. The **doer** is in the oblique — the same **min, te, wî, wê, me, we, wan** you know from *navê min* — and the verb is the **past stem**:

- *Min nan xwar.* I ate bread.
- *Te çi kir?* What did you do?
- *Wî çay vexwar.* He drank tea.
- *Me ew dît.* We saw him.

A noun doer is oblique too: a feminine one takes -ê (*Xezalê got …* Xezal said …), a plural -an (*zarokan got …* the children said …); masculine names usually stay as they are (*Hamo got …*).

The past stems: *xwar* (ate) · *vexwar* (drank) · *kir* (did) · *got* (said) · *dît* (saw) · *da* (gave) · *anî* (brought) · *bir* (took away) · *xwest* (wanted).

Not: *Min nexwar.* I didn’t eat. · *Wê negot.* She didn’t say.

skills.grammarMd:
In the transitive past the verb agrees with the **object**, not with the doer:

- *Min sêvek xwar.* I ate an apple. · *Min du sêv xwarin.* I ate two apples. (**-in** for a plural object)
- *Wî ez dîtim.* He saw me. (**-im**: the object is *ez*)
- *Min tu dîtî.* I saw you.
- *Me hûn dîtin.* We saw you (all).

So the object goes into the direct form (*ez, tu, ew, em, hûn*) and the doer into the oblique (*min, te, wî, wê, me, we, wan*) — the opposite of the present: *Ez te dibînim* / *Min tu dîtî*.

More past stems: *dot* (milked) · *çêkir* (made) · *pijand* (cooked) · *şûşt* (washed) · *xwend* (read) · *nivîsî* (wrote) · *kirî* (bought).

skills.titleEn: I was eating, I was going
skills.grammarMd:
For what **was happening** or **used to happen**, put **di-** before the past stem:

- *Ez diçûm.* I was going / I used to go.
- *Min nan dixwar.* I was eating bread.
- *Dapîr her havîn dihat vir.* Grandma used to come here every summer.
- *Wan stran digotin.* They were singing songs.

The agreement rules stay the same: intransitive with the subject, transitive with the object.

Two at once: *Dema ku me nan dixwar, Zerê hat.* While we were eating, Zerê came.

Negative: **ne-** before di-: *Min nedizanî.* I didn’t know. · *Em nediçûn wir.* We didn’t use to go there.

skills.grammarMd:
A real story mixes the two pasts — check each verb:

- *Ez çûm mêrgê û min Zerê dît.* I went to the meadow and saw Zerê. (*çûn* intransitive → *ez*; *dîtin* transitive → *min*)
- *Em rûniştin û me nan xwar.* We sat down and ate bread.

Questions: *Te çi kir?* What did you do? · *Kê got?* Who said (it)? (**kê** is the oblique of *kî*) · *Çi qewimî?* What happened?

To tell **someone**, use **ji … re**: *Min ji te re got.* I told you. · *Xezalê ji diya xwe re got.* Xezal told her mother.

And to tell a whole tale, *vegotin*: *Hamo çîrokek vegot.* Hamo told a story.
